questions.q: What is the single most important diagnostic step for this bug?
options: Clicking the card and checking which exact measure populates its Values well in the Fields pane
Reading the card's title text, since that always matches the bound measure
Rebuilding the whole report from a blank page
Deleting the Drill-Down page to simplify comparison
questions.explain: A visual's title is just typed text with no guaranteed relationship to which measure actually feeds it — the Fields pane binding is the real source of truth.

questions.q: How is the hypothesis confirmed, rather than just assumed?
options: By adding a test card explicitly bound to [Total Sales] and confirming it changes correctly with the region filter, matching the Drill-Down page
By asking the Operations Manager to trust the explanation without proof
By checking the DAX syntax for typos
By comparing the color of the two cards
questions.explain: A controlled test — changing one variable (which measure is bound) and observing the predicted result — confirms the diagnosis.

questions.q: What does ALL ( TerritoryDim ) inside Total Sales (All Regions) remove, that explains the symptom?
options: Any filter currently applied through the TerritoryDim relationship, including the page's own Region slicer
All rows from the Fact table entirely
Only filters applied through the Date table
Nothing — ALL() has no effect on slicers
questions.explain: ALL(TerritoryDim) strips filters flowing through that relationship, which is exactly why the card ignores the Region slicer.

questions.q: Why did Total Sales and Total Sales (All Regions) look identical when the Executive Summary page was first built and reviewed in Lesson 7?
options: With no region filter applied, ALL(TerritoryDim) has nothing to strip away, so both measures coincidentally match
They are actually the same DAX formula with two different names
Power BI automatically synced their values at build time
The bug didn't exist yet at that point
questions.explain: The coincidental match in the unfiltered state is exactly why the mis-binding went unnoticed until a region filter was actually applied.

questions.q: Why is this described as a binding mistake rather than a formula mistake?
options: Total Sales (All Regions) is a legitimate, correctly-written measure still needed elsewhere — the error is which measure a specific visual is wired to
There is no real distinction between the two
The DAX for Total Sales (All Regions) actually contains a syntax error
Power Query, not DAX, caused the issue
questions.explain: The measure itself is correct and still serves Pct of Company Total; the problem is purely which measure the Executive Summary card happens to reference.
